updates.title: AWS adds Neptune Graph Sessions for agent workloads
updates.whatChanged: AWS adds Neptune Graph Sessions on 27 November for Neptune Analytics graphs. The compute mode scales memory and CPU and bills for memory used. Graphs start at 4 or 8 s-NCU, include up to twice that memory headroom, scale to zero after 15 idle minutes, and resume in seconds with data retained.
updates.whyCare: You can isolate a GraphRAG conversation or agent task without keeping a provisioned graph at its 16 m-NCU minimum. Compare session compute with shared graph stores or vector-only retrieval for isolation, query, and cost.
updates.before: Provisioned Neptune graphs required a 16 m-NCU minimum. Teams kept separate graphs running for conversations or tasks.
updates.after: Neptune Graph Sessions start at 4 or 8 s-NCU and adjust memory and CPU automatically. They scale to zero after 15 idle minutes and retain graph data.
updates.learn: Prototype with representative GraphRAG or agent queries. Measure memory growth, resume latency, and cost against a shared graph or vector store. Check regional availability and limits in the Neptune Analytics documentation.

sources.name: AWS What's New - Amazon Neptune introduces Neptune Graph Sessions

updates.architectureImplication: Design graph state around tasks and allow for resume delay after idle scale-down. Keep durable shared knowledge separate from per-task graphs. Compare isolation and cost with shared graphs or vector-only retrieval.
heldReasons: Fact check: The item says teams previously kept separate graphs running for conversations or tasks. | The sources say separate graphs fit agentic and per-user workloads, and that provisioned graphs remain available, but they do not say that teams kept such graphs running before this feature.
